result.issue: AMC-1507 — P1: Preserve nested failures and branch provenance when importing Pi v3 sessions (In Review, child of AMC-1505)

claims.claim: Implementation commits c050244a, 8defa070 and 1b89a573 (and qualification point d1f2ee84) are on the integration branch at 6e7875f2
claims.evidence: git merge-base --is-ancestor for each of c050244a, 8defa070, 1b89a573, d1f2ee84 against HEAD 6e7875f21bb6b30bc0f1a32713deb3bc6a7cad2f: all four report ancestor=yes. git log on src/importers/piSessionImport.ts shows c050244a -> 8defa070 -> 1b89a573 -> bda990ac -> 822123d7 -> d3cae563.

claims.claim: Versioned Pi session JSONL is detected explicitly; v1/v2/other versions are refused by name with no generic-success fallback
claims.evidence: src/importers/piSessionImport.ts:87-102 (detectPiSession: header type 'session', version===3 supported, otherwise unsupported with named version; non-numeric version labelled 'with an invalid version field'), :134-138 (parseDetectedPiSession throws PiSessionFormatError on unsupported, never returns generic path); src/importers/neutralImporter.ts:528-532 (Pi parse happens before generic parseFile; PiSessionFormatError surfaces as an unsupported/malformed entry). tests/piSessionImport.test.ts:178-200 ('unsupported session version ... no generic fallback' for versions 1/2/4, and 'invalid version value ... without echoing source values') passed in this run.

claims.claim: Nested tool failures (message.isError) and model errors/cancellation (stopReason error/aborted, errorMessage) are preserved and reach the Watch failure index; length-truncation is flagged, not failed
claims.evidence: src/importers/piSessionImport.ts:32 (FAILED_STOP_REASONS = error, aborted), :314-317 and :328-329 (assistant error/errorMessage), :336 (truncated: stopReason==='length'), :350-358 (toolResult isError -> error + errorMessage). tests/piSessionImport.test.ts:76 'nested tool and model failures reach the Watch failure index' and :155 'aborted counts as a failure; length-truncated is flagged, not failed' passed.

claims.claim: Tool-call IDs, resolved tool names, provider/model identity and original entry/parent IDs are preserved
claims.evidence: src/importers/piSessionImport.ts:292-299 (entryId, parentId, ancestryComplete, onCurrentPath, sessionParent, sourceFormat in metadata), :333-334 (model, providerId), :342-349 and :362-363 (toolCallId, tool name from message.toolName or resolved from the calling assistant's toolCall block). tests/piSessionImport.test.ts:85 passed.

claims.claim: Structural header/label/compaction entries remain source metadata, never invented successful executions; discarded branches are kept as data but marked off the current path, not replayed as current context
claims.evidence: src/importers/piSessionImport.ts:27-30 (STRUCTURAL_TYPES), :224 (counted as entries.structural), :311-312 (traces derived only from type==='message'), :277-281 and :297 (leaf = last well-formed entry, onCurrentPath computed by walking parentId), :232 (offPathEntries). tests/piSessionImport.test.ts:104 'structural entries stay metadata' and :125 'a discarded branch is kept as data but marked off the current path' passed; :147 'a forked session keeps its parent provenance' passed (forkedFrom from header.parentSession, :235).

claims.claim: Missing timing stays unknown and is never presented as measured zero latency; ingestion average uses only measured samples
claims.evidence: src/importers/piSessionImport.ts:304-305 (durationMs: null, comment 'Pi persists timestamps, never durations'); src/agents/traceIngestion.ts:31 (durationMs: number | null), :33 (timestamp: number | null), :81 and :127 (avgLatencyMs: number | null, initial null), :139-140 (running mean over measuredLatencyCount only). Mutation: changing piSessionImport.ts 'durationMs: null' to 'durationMs: 0' made tests/piSessionImport.test.ts 'missing timing is unknown, never a measured zero' FAIL (1 failed | 10 passed); source restored and confirmed byte-identical. tests/traceIngestionTiming.test.ts 3/3 passed.

claims.claim: Imported data retains SELF_REPORTED provenance, redaction (including sanitized identities that do not leak secrets) and the source digest
claims.evidence: src/importers/neutralImporter.ts:666 (sourceTrust: 'SELF_REPORTED', evaluation: 'NOT_EVALUATED'); src/importers/piSessionImport.ts:172-204 (sanitizePiSession: ids that the redactor changed or that use the reserved prefix become namespace-separated sha256 markers; toolCallId and toolCall block ids handled). tests/piSessionImport.test.ts:202 'provenance stays self-reported and redacted, with the source digest' passed. Mutation: making safeId return the raw value made tests/piSessionImportBoundaries.test.ts fail 2 tests ('sanitized header, entry and tool IDs ... without leaking source secrets' and 'reserved safe-ID collisions ...'), 2 failed | 12 passed; source restored.

claims.claim: Cycle/duplicate-ID termination and orphan handling from the 2026-09-08 review are resolved: duplicates and cycles refuse import, orphans keep failures with incomplete ancestry
claims.evidence: src/importers/piSessionImport.ts:150-169 (inspectTree: duplicate id -> PiSessionFormatError; iterative bounded walk with per-entry path set -> cyclic ancestry refused; ancestryComplete map), :234 (orphanedEntries), :144 (orphan warning). tests/piSessionImportBoundaries.test.ts:50 'duplicate entry IDs are explicitly unsupported with no generic fallback' and :129 'an orphan retains its failure with incomplete ancestry and no inferred user input' passed.

claims.claim: Timestamp validity: malformed/rolled-over dates are rejected rather than parsed permissively; valid explicit epoch values (including zero) are retained

defectsFound.description: entryTimestamp accepts any finite numeric timestamp, including negative (pre-1970) values, while the generic mapper traceMapping.traceTimestamp (src/importers/traceMapping.ts:18) rejects value < 0 and > 8.64e15. Pi writes ISO strings so numeric input is unlikely, but a Pi entry with timestamp -1 would be recorded as a valid 1969 event time by one mapper and as unknown by the other. Boundary inconsistency, no test covers negative numeric Pi timestamps.
